one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 FY2027 results (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected around 2026-11-18 to 11-25 (Q3 FY26 was reported 2025-11-19, 25 days after quarter end; the date is not yet announced). Street EPS 4.33 (Zacks, 4 est.), whisper 4.55 (80% 4.24-4.86); my build 5.03 on EBITDA ~304 at the top of the 281-302 guide. The company has beaten its EBITDA guide 6 of 6 quarters, so a beat is likely, but the stock reacts to the outlook: Q4 seasonality, any FY28 colour after AT&T's lowered 2027-28 capex (2026-10-21) and MasTec's Communications deferrals (2026-10-29), and whether the $150M wireless deferral holds. The Q2 beat-and-raise still fell ~25% in a week. So a near-symmetric distribution: median ~$222.5 (+0.7%: likely beat and oversold at a 52-week low with September insider buying, against negative momentum and sector de-rating), lognormal sigma 16% (annual 53%/3.5 = 15% plus a little for the print).

model_inputs.ebit_basis_note: EBIT = GAAP operating income + amortization of intangibles (the company's Adjusted EPS excludes only amortization; SBC is a cost). Check Q2 FY27: revenue 2,005.9 - costs 1,813.9 = 192.0 + amortization 60.5 = 252.5 = segment adjusted EBITDA 315.5 - depreciation 55.2 - SBC 10.3 + 2.4 (gain on asset sales 2.3 and other items, which adjusted EBITDA takes out and other income carries). Segment 'ebit' rows hold segment ADJUSTED EBITDA; corporate_ebit = -(depreciation + SBC) + 2.5 a quarter; da = depreciation only (ex amortization), so engine EBITDA = adjusted EBITDA - SBC + ~2.5. SBC is already deducted inside corporate_ebit (sbc_rate 0.53% of revenue), so years[].sbc_pct_rev is 0 to count it exactly once.

drivers.derivation: Agent 3 (skeptic) path, differs from the approved set: actual quarters unchanged (Ex.99.1 backlog tables). horizon_multiples.peer_basis: Whole-company peer median 18.65x NTM P/E (MTZ 16.59, PRIM 17.1, MYRG 20.2, PWR 35.2; Zacks consensus, company-adjusted EPS). Own NTM P/E 12.13x (221.05 / (0.25 x Zacks FY27 15.98 + 0.75 x FY28 18.98) = 221.05/18.23). Exit rule 18.65 x (12.13/18.65)^0.8 = 13.22x, less a net 0.53 turns for post-horizon risks (long_dated_risks) = 12.7x on the build's adjusted (ex-amortization, SBC-costed) NTM EPS.

Mid-cycle cross-check on trailing EBITDA (GAAP operating income + D&A, the secfacts basis): whole-company peers with a filed trailing figure PRIM 14.5x, MYRG 13.2x (median 13.85x); DY own pro-forma trailing ~8.9x (EV 9,147 = 221.05 x 30.16M + net debt 2,479.7 over TTM adj. EBITDA 959.8 - SBC 38.1 + ~110 for the five Power Solutions months not in the TTM = ~1,030). Exit rule 13.85 x (8.9/13.85)^0.8 = 9.72x, less ~0.4 turns (same post-horizon risks, scaled) = 9.3x, applied to LTM EBITDA at the horizon (a trailing multiple on a trailing figure, so not on a peak forward year).

downside.story: 10th percentile: a carrier program cut on top of the October 2026 capex resets. AT&T (20.1% of revenue) spends at the low end of its lowered $22-23B and Verizon/Frontier (10.4%) reorganises spend, the ~$150M wireless deferral does not come back in FY28, and DY's Communications NTM backlog ends up 10% below my base (MasTec's Communications backlog fell 7.5% in one quarter). Communications margin -175bp (MasTec's fell 370bp y/y on deferrals; 2018-19 DY precedent), the data-center cycle pauses for a year (Building Systems share -20%, margin -300bp back to mid-teens, Power Solutions' first guide). The market pays ~10x NTM EPS, the low end of the cycle range.

upside.story: 90th percentile: the deferral returns in FY28 with BEAD construction and long-haul/middle-mile awards converting (>$1B contracted, $20B TAM), NTM backlog 8% above my base (about the approved set's path), Communications margin back to FY26 levels (+100bp), Building Systems keeps share in a data-center market growing with hyperscaler capex (+15%), and the multiple re-rates to ~15.7x as the October AI-infrastructure sell-off reverses (still below the 18.65x peer median).

comps_summary.peer_range: Whole-company NTM P/E 16.59x (MTZ) to 35.2x (PWR); segment-only Building Systems peers EME 18.52, FIX 19.11, STRL 13.9, LMB 10.0 (median 16.2x). Trailing EV/EBITDA (filings) PRIM 14.5x, MYRG 13.2x, STRL 11.5x, LMB 10.0x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: DY own NTM P/E 12.13x (Zacks) is 35% below the 18.65x whole-company median. Exit rule (k 0.8) gives 13.22x; I use 12.7x after a net -0.53 turns of post-horizon risk, below the whole range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount the shrink rule keeps is the market's and I keep it (k 0.8, no argued change): DY is a single-end-market telecom contractor with top-3 customers ~36% of revenue and ~35% of receivables (incl. Lumen 13.4% of receivables at B2/B), carriers just cut 2027-28 capex budgets, and FTTH spending likely peaks before 2030; the extra -0.53 turns are the costed long_dated_risks.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 8 peers, 4 whole-company (MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) and 4 Building Systems segment-only (EME, FIX, STRL, LMB). model_inputs.structure_note: Value sits in two horizon-multiple legs on the quarterly backlog-and-capacity driver build: 70% NTM P/E on the build's own adjusted (ex-amortization, SBC-costed) EPS at 2027-11-02 and 30% LTM EV/EBITDA as the mid-cycle cross-check (playbook range 0.2-0.3). The driver build is the approved set's structure (Communications = conversion x prior NTM backlog; Building Systems = US private data-center construction x DY share), with my own skeptic values on four drivers (comms_ntm_backlog, comms_conv Q3 FY27, comms_margin, bs_margin; bs_share unchanged). No DCF leg (not a neocloud). Weights are judgment, not tested.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) supplier finance obligations $349.4M (Q1 FY27; source 19) added to net debt as debt-like (playbook trap); excluding them adds ~$11.6/share; I could not open 10-Q note 22 myself (sec.gov refuses a generic User-Agent and WebFetch truncated), so the Q2 figure ($367.4M per the 10-09 round) is not used. (2) My comms_ntm_backlog path (~6%/yr) sits below the approved set (~10%/yr): about -$20 to -25/share vs the set; driver values differ from the approved set by design (my independent view), the supervisor uses the approved drivers. (3) Interest is charged at 5.5% on net debt including supplier finance, which is not interest-bearing in the P&L: conservative by ~$0.45 EPS a year. (4) No equity raise modelled: the March 2026 automatic S-3 shelf (source 20) has no announced use; pro-forma net leverage ~2.3x and FCF cover the build, so P(raise by the horizon) <20% (my estimate ~10%), named here, not in financing_events. (5) Bolt-on M&A cash (NTI $226M in Q2) is not modelled in other_uses since no revenue is added for it either.
model_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 12.7x NTM P/E on a business with a ~10% after-tax cost of equity implies roughly 2-3% long-run EPS growth after FY2029 at a ~13% Communications / ~19% Building Systems margin, i.e. the market (and I) price the FTTH build as peaking around 2028-30 with BEAD/long-haul and data-center work only partly replacing it.

reasoning: Lane: skeptic. The 61% fall from $566 is mostly a sector de-rating (MasTec -56%, Comfort Systems -42% and EMCOR -28% from their 52-week highs) plus three DY-specific hits: the August Communications cut (~$150M wireless into FY28, margin -134bp), AT&T's lowered 2027-28 capex outlook on 2026-10-21 (the day of DY's new low), and MasTec's 2026-10-29 Communications slump on customer deferrals. I searched for a fresh short report, downgrade or credit event and found none in 2026: the only short report is Spruce Point's from February 2025 (DSO, Frontier dealings, accounting; rebutted by Raymond James), the VIC/Coffee Capital bear case from December 2025 is a cycle-peak argument (FTTH capex peaks 2026-27, >66% of revenue from five customers), Moody's has DY at Ba2, and insiders bought in September. Red flags I would weigh: receivables up 34% in six months; Lumen at 13.4% of receivables vs ~5% of revenue at B2/B; ~$350M supplier finance (added to net debt); Building Systems margin helped by estimate changes. Model: the approved quarterly driver structure with my values. comms_ntm_backlog grows ~6%/yr (set ~10%), Q3 conversion trimmed for the deferral, Communications margin held flat (set +20-30bp/yr), Building Systems margin 19% (set 20%), bs_share unchanged. FY28 EPS ~18.3 vs Zacks 18.98 (-4%) and StockAnalysis 20.77 (-12%); FY29 ~20.3 vs 22.37 (-9%). Valuation: 12.7x NTM P/E (exit rule from own 12.1x toward an 18.65x 4-peer median, less 0.53 turns for post-horizon risks) and 9.3x LTM EBITDA, $255 research target (12m), +16% vs $221. Weighed honestly, the downside case is real but already largely in the price: at 12x NTM, the stock discounts roughly my downside drivers without the multiple compression. Downside $123 (P10) and upside $399 (P90) give a fatter left tail, consistent with 53% realized volatility. Research limits: sec.gov refused a generic User-Agent (I followed the brief and did not send an email), so 10-Q notes were read via WebFetch, which truncated; the Q2 supplier-finance figure and debt covenants were not confirmed. Twelve Data insider data needs a paid plan. Not driver-linked: none (no custom legs).
